verdict.rationale:
Fivetran documents a dedicated 'Alerts' feature in its dashboard (fivetran-docs-15) and its MCP server exposes read-only queries like 'was my last postgres sync successful' and 'are any of my connections broken' (fivetran-docs-28, fivetran-docs-59), which supports freshness/cadence checking programmatically. However, the evidence gives only a bare feature title for Alerts with no detail on configuring expected-cadence thresholds or proactive notification mechanics, and the MCP tool is a pull-based query rather than a push alert.

missing for 10: documentation of configurable freshness/SLA thresholds per table, proactive push notifications (email/Slack/webhook) tied to missed sync cadence, and independent/hands-on confirmation that alerts fire reliably when a pipeline misses its schedule.
